problems.detail:
New false statement in run.py. The comment above README_PY_LABELS (run.py, check 1's section header block) justifies the new five-label rule with "because the checks that read them -- check 2 reads imports: and used by:, check 10 reads venv: -- lose the file silently when its line is gone". Check 2 does not lose the file silently: it reports the missing line by name. Verified in a scratch copy of 3d199b1 (git archive | tar -x, baseline `selfcheck: 31 python files, 0 problems`): deleting only the `imports:` line of the `eval/score_run.py` entry, keeping the header, prints

  check 1: README entry 'eval/score_run.py' carries no imports: line (contracts 0.1's five-line format)
  check 2: eval/score_run.py has no imports: line

Only check 10 is silent (verified separately: deleting the `venv:` line of `data/environments/appworld.py` while `import definitely_not_a_module` sits in that file drops all three check-10 lines). The comment is the stated reason for a rule a later agent may revisit, and it credits check 2 with a hole it does not have.

Nothing about the code changes.

problems.detail: New statement in README.md section 3 that selfcheck does not back. The added preamble reads "... adds the new file's name to the `used by:` line of every repo file it imports; where such a line is written as a brace list, `train/methods/{ctool,cgen,cparam}.py`, the new name widens the brace list rather than standing beside it. `run.py selfcheck` compares those lines against the real import graph, so it is the check that catches a recipe followed half way." The approved fix's rationale says an extender "who appends a separate path instead of widening the brace list still fails check 2". That is false: `_split_top_level` splits the line on the top-level comma first and `_expand_braces` runs per fragment, so the separate-path form yields the same set. Verified in a scratch copy that had recipe 2 followed to green (`selfcheck: 32 python files, 0 problems`): rewriting README.md:250 as `used by: train/methods/{ctool,cgen,cparam}.py, train/methods/cseq.py` and README.md:287 the same way still prints `selfcheck: 32 python files, 0 problems`, rc=0. An extender who reads the paragraph as a selfcheck requirement is told something the check never tests.
problems.fix: Separate the two claims in that sentence: keep "adds the new file's name to the `used by:` line of every repo file it imports" as what selfcheck catches, and either drop the brace-list clause or mark it as the house spelling that selfcheck accepts either way -- e.g. "a line written as a brace list, `train/methods/{ctool,cgen,cparam}.py`, is widened rather than extended with a second fragment; selfcheck reads both spellings the same, this one keeps the line short."

problems.detail:
Check 2's by-name test reads the wrong file on an `imports:` line, and the rewritten message now asserts that wrong direction. In `_check_by_name_fragments` (run.py), the non-placeholder branch always treats `path_text` as the importer: `prefix = _dynamic_import_prefix(current_file)` and `_has_dynamic_import_of(path_text, prefix, _module_name(current_file))`. That is right for a `used by:` line (the annotated file is the import target, `path_text` is the importer) and backwards for an `imports:` line (the annotated file is the importer, `path_text` is the target) -- the placeholder branch two lines above gets the `imports:` direction right, testing `current_file` with the prefix derived from `path_text`. Verified on a scratch copy of 3d199b1: replacing `data/environments/__init__.py`'s `imports: none (repo); [importlib, PyYAML]` with the truthful `imports: data/environments/appworld.py (by name, inside open_env); [importlib, PyYAML]` prints

  check 2: data/environments/__init__.py imports: by-name entry data/environments/appworld.py holds no importlib.import_module call naming data.environments.<module>
  selfcheck: 31 python files, 1 problems

so a correct annotation is reported as a defect. The wrong direction was in the pre-fix `_has_dynamic_import_call(path_text)` too, but the SC-3 rewrite touched exactly this line and hardened the assumption into the prefix and the message text. Latent today: no `imports:` line carries a non-placeholder by-name fragment.
problems.fix: Branch on the label the way the placeholder branch already does. On an `imports:` line the annotated file is the importer, so test `_has_dynamic_import_of(current_file, _dynamic_import_prefix(path_text), _module_name(path_text))` and word the message as "<current_file> holds no importlib.import_module call naming <prefix><module>". On a `used by:` line keep today's `_has_dynamic_import_of(path_text, _dynamic_import_prefix(current_file), _module_name(current_file))` and today's message.

problems.detail: README.md section 3 (the preamble added at README.md:329-335, and recipes 6 and 7 at README.md:367-381). The fix's own claim for pipeline-review-skills:W6-L15-2 is that a recipe followed literally now ends green, and the new preamble states the whole annotation obligation as "writes that file's own five annotation lines into section 2 above, and adds the new file's name to the `used by:` line of every repo file it imports". That is the import-graph half of check 2 only. Check 2 has a second obligation the sentence does not name: `_check_package_marker` (run.py:1032-1046) requires an `(as their package)` used-by line to equal the .py files of its own directory, and two such lines exist (README.md:169 for models/agent_models/__init__.py, README.md:190 for models/probe_models/__init__.py). Recipes 6 and 7 both add a file into one of those directories, and both kinds of new file import no repo file at all (models/probe_models/qwen.py is `imports: none (repo); [transformers]`, models/agent_models/gptoss.py is `imports: none (repo); [openai_harmony, ...]`), so the preamble's rule gives the extender nothing to do and the marker line is never widened. Verified in a scratch copy of fix/2026-09-20-wave6-selfcheck (baseline `selfcheck: 31 python files, 0 problems`, rc=0). Recipe 6: added models/probe_models/qwen2.py with a column-zero LORA_TARGETS plus its five README annotation lines -> `check 2: models/probe_models/__init__.py used by: package marker names ['models/probe_models/base.py', 'models/probe_models/qwen.py', 'models/probe_models/service.py'], directory models/probe_models holds ['models/probe_models/base.py', 'models/probe_models/qwen.py', 'models/probe_models/qwen2.py', 'models/probe_models/service.py']` / `selfcheck: 32 python files, 1 problems`, rc=1. Recipe 7: added models/agent_models/llama.py with column-zero STOP, EFFORTS, DEFAULT_EFFORT, DEFAULT_DATE plus its five annotation lines -> `check 2: models/agent_models/__init__.py used by: package marker names ['models/agent_models/gptoss.py', 'models/agent_models/service.py'], directory models/agent_models holds ['models/agent_models/gptoss.py', 'models/agent_models/llama.py', 'models/agent_models/service.py']` / `selfcheck: 32 python files, 1 problems`, rc=1. The other two recipes the same edit touched do end green: recipe 2 followed literally (train/methods/cseq.py with VERSION, VERSION_HISTORY under the rule block, PROBE_KIND, CHECKPOINT_META; "cseq" on AXES['probe.method']; PROBE_KIND + MATCH_VERSION + match_cseq in eval/utils/probe_eval.py; the five annotation lines; the two brace lists widened) gives `selfcheck: 32 python files, 0 problems`, rc=0, and recipe 1 followed literally (data/environments/toy.py with INSTRUCTIONS, SPLIT_ROLE, VERSION, VERSION_HISTORY under the rule block; "toy" on AXES['data.env']; the five annotation lines; toy.py added to data/environments/__init__.py's used by: line) gives `selfcheck: 32 python files, 0 problems`, rc=0. So the fixer's summary sentence "Recipe 7 carried the same omission as 1, 2 and 6 and was closed in the same edit" holds for the column-zero bindings but not for the annotation work, and the preamble's claim that selfcheck "is the check that catches a recipe followed half way" now describes a recipe that is itself half way.

Keep it one sentence in the preamble rather than repeating it in recipes 6 and 7, matching how the brace-list rule is already written there. Re-verify by repeating the two experiments above: with the marker line widened, each gives `selfcheck: 32 python files, 0 problems`, rc=0.

problems.detail: run.py:938-940, `_dynamic_import_prefix`. It builds the dotted package as `".".join(Path(annotated_file).parent.parts) + "."`, which is right for a file inside a package but wrong for a file at the repo root: `_dynamic_import_prefix('run.py')` returns `'.'` (verified on the fix branch: `python -c "import run; print(repr(run._dynamic_import_prefix('run.py')))"` -> `'.'`). The correct prefix for a root-level module is the empty string, since its dotted name has no package part. With `'.'`, the f-string arm of `_has_dynamic_import_of` (run.py:955-963) demands a leading constant starting with a dot, which no `importlib.import_module(f"run...")` call would have, so a correct dynamic import of a root-level module would be reported as missing; only the `exact` arm (`_module_name('run.py')` -> `'run'`) would still accept the plain-string spelling. This is latent on today's tree -- run.py is the only root-level .py file and no `(by name)` annotation names it -- so nothing fires now; it is the same class of latent arithmetic error as the already-fixed `_resolve_versions_entry` two-template bug.
problems.fix: Derive the prefix from the module's own dotted name instead of joining path parts unconditionally: in `_dynamic_import_prefix`, return `""` when `Path(annotated_file).parent.parts` is empty and the joined package plus a dot otherwise -- e.g. `parts = Path(annotated_file).parent.parts; return ".".join(parts) + "." if parts else ""`. Every prefix in use today (`data.environments.`, `models.agent_models.`, `models.probe_models.`) is unchanged, so `run.py selfcheck` stays at `31 python files, 0 problems`; the failure message's `{prefix}<module>` tail then reads `<module>` for a root-level file, which is correct.

cannotVerify: Check 11's breakage (`touch <scratch>/experimental_settings/free.yaml`) could not be run: the read-only hook refuses any Bash command line naming experimental_settings/<x>.yaml together with rm, and the ticket's own undo is `rm -rf` of the whole scratch copy, which the hook also refuses when the command names that path. That half is verified by reading run.py:1320-1333 and by the stage-table listing, which names models/probe_models/qwen.py and models/agent_models/gptoss.py among its 22 files, so the recipes' new 'because the stage table names this file' clauses are true.

`"$PR -m unittest"` from the tree root runs 0 tests (`Ran 0 tests in 0.000s / OK`, rc=0) on the fix branch. tests/ holds test_packed_loss.py and test_registry_concurrent_append.py, and README.md:322 says to run the latter as a script (`external/probe-env/bin/python tests/test_registry_concurrent_append.py`), not through unittest discovery. tests/ is byte-identical to f810f9f, so this is the state the fix inherited, not a regression it caused; I did not treat it as a problem of this branch.

ownerQuestions: With an empty prefix, a root-level by-name target passes the f-string arm of `_has_dynamic_import_of` for any `importlib.import_module` f-string, since ast sees only that the call names some top-level module; only the plain-string spelling is still tested exactly. problems.detail:
New false statements introduced by the GR4 fix. .claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:100-105 now says: "The line `run.py: launched <run_id>; monitor with ...` is the only success signal, and the call exits 0 either way. A launch that fails prints no such line — often nothing at all, since the probe service's `check` client is the only launch step that writes to the terminal — tears the run's service pieces down and appends a `launch_failed` finish row. Read Phase 5's `ls` line for that row...". Three of those claims are false for jobs/launch.py's own refusal paths, which are the common way a launch fails.

(a) `jobs/launch.launch` leaves the process through `sys.exit(<string>)` at jobs/launch.py:743 (the launch gate refusal), :779, :795 and :820 (`_no_cards_message`, jobs/launch.py:558-563) and :672 (the endpoint file did not appear). `sys.exit` with a string writes that string to stderr and exits 1, so the call neither exits 0 nor prints nothing, and the probe service's `check` client (jobs/launch.py:895-899) is not the only launch step that writes to the terminal. The dirty-tree refusal the skill itself describes in Phase 2 is another one (jobs/launch.py:174).

(b) Worse, `registry.append_start(start_row)` is at jobs/launch.py:857, after the piece-placement loop that holds the three `_no_cards_message` exits (:779, :795, :820) and after the gate refusal (:743). On those four paths there is no start row at all, and run.py:1865-1869 (the only place a `launch_failed` row is written) is never reached because `launch.launch` never returns. So for the most common launch failure — no host has enough free cards — nothing appears in `run.py ls`, there is no `launch_failed` row, and `<run_dir>/log/<piece index>.txt` does not exist either. An operator following the new paragraph looks in two places that are both empty and has already been told to ignore the exit code, while the actual diagnosis was printed on stderr.

The `outcome != "up"` case the paragraph describes (run.py:1865-1871, reached only after the start row exists) is real, but it is one branch of the failure set, not the whole of it. Verified by reading jobs/launch.py and run.py on the fix branch; no launch was run.
problems.fix: Rewrite .claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:100-105 to split the two failure shapes instead of stating one as universal. Something like: "`run.py: launched <run_id>; monitor with ...` is the only success signal. A launch can fail in two shapes. `jobs/launch.py` refuses before the start row is written — the launch gate, a host with too few free cards, an endpoint file that never appeared — and each of those prints its own `jobs/launch.py: ...` line and exits 1, leaving no registry row and nothing in `ls`; read that line. A piece that starts and then fails its alive check is the silent shape: the call prints nothing more and exits 0, the run's service pieces are torn down and a `launch_failed` finish row is appended. Read Phase 5's `ls` line for that row and `<run_dir>/log/<piece index>.txt` for why the piece died." (Citations: jobs/launch.py:743, :779/:795/:820, :672, :857; run.py:1865-1871; jobs/launch.py:758 for the log path.)

problems.detail:
The GR4 fix (`.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:100-109`) splits a failed launch into two shapes and puts "a service endpoint file that never appeared" in the first one: "`jobs/launch.py` refuses before the start row is written — the Phase 2 dirty-tree gate, the launch gate, a host with too few free cards, a service endpoint file that never appeared — and each of those refusals prints its own `jobs/launch.py: ...` line and exits 1, leaving no registry row, nothing in Phase 5's `ls` and no piece log". Three of the four items are right; the endpoint item is false on every clause, and it is the one case where the skill's advice leaves cards held.

Read off the code on this base: `_wait_for_endpoint` (jobs/launch.py:664-672, `sys.exit(f"jobs/launch.py: {path} did not appear within launch_timeout_s")`) is called at jobs/launch.py:894, inside `launch()` for `stage == "inject"` only. By then `registry.append_start(start_row)` has already run at jobs/launch.py:857 with `"status": "launching"` (jobs/launch.py:855), the lock has been released (the `with registry.lock():` block ends at jobs/launch.py:868), the log directory has been made (`_ensure_log_dir`, jobs/launch.py:871), the service pieces have been started (jobs/launch.py:885-887) and their alive check has passed (jobs/launch.py:887-890). So the start row exists, the run shows in `run.py ls` as an open row, `<run_dir>/log/<piece index>.txt` exists for each started service piece, and — unlike every other failure path in `launch()`, which calls `teardown_services` before returning (jobs/launch.py:878, 889, 900, 907) — this `sys.exit` tears nothing down: the agent and probe services stay alive on their cards. A second launch of the same key is then refused by the launch gate while the row is younger than `launch_timeout_s` and no piece has beaten (jobs/launch.py:251-265).

An operator following the paragraph reads the printed `jobs/launch.py: ... did not appear` line, believes nothing was recorded and nothing started, and leaves live vLLM and probe services holding cards plus an open `launching` row behind.

problems.detail: `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:110-115` (added by c17d75c) says the third launch-failure shape is "An `inject` launch whose probe service never writes its endpoint file", and tells the operator that shape leaves an open `launching` row, the piece logs and "the service pieces alive on their cards — end them with Phase 6b's `kill`". That trigger belongs to the second (quiet) shape, not the third. `launch()` runs `alive_check(service_pieces, window_s=launch_timeout_s, poll_s=5)` at `jobs/launch.py:887`, and a `service` piece passes that check only when `(run_dir / p["endpoint_file"]).exists()` **and** its port answers (`jobs/launch.py:432-433`). So a probe service that never writes `service_probe_0.json` fails there: `jobs/launch.py:888-890` calls `teardown_services(run_dir)` and returns `"alive_check"`, `run.py:2040-2046` appends the `launch_failed` finish row and `return "stop"` with the call exiting 0 — services torn down, no `launching` row, nothing for `kill` to end. `_wait_for_endpoint` (`jobs/launch.py:664-672`) is reached only at `jobs/launch.py:894`, i.e. after that check already proved the file exists, so its `sys.exit(f"jobs/launch.py: {path} did not appear within launch_timeout_s")` can fire only when the already-existing file never parses into a dict with a truthy `base_url` (`jobs/launch.py:669`) — and `models/probe_models/service.py:53-62` writes `base_url` into that file atomically (tmp + replace), so in normal operation the third shape is unreachable. An operator whose probe service failed to come up therefore follows the skill to a live-cards/`kill` diagnosis that is the opposite of what happened.

problems.detail: `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:216-218` (added by 687b685) says that when the setting and stage carry a real run, "all three act on that real run: ... `retry` clears its markers and launches it again." `retry` does not launch a run whose pieces are still live, and it clears the markers before it finds that out. `cmd_retry` (`run.py:731-741`) calls `_clear_continue_markers(stage, run_dir)` at `run.py:739` unconditionally — before the dirty-tree gate, before the launch gate, before any liveness test — and `_clear_continue_markers` (`run.py:693-707`) unlinks `done.json` and `consumed.json`, and for `train` also `train_log.jsonl`, `train_done.json`, `align_check.json` and the whole `last/` directory (`shutil.rmtree`). Only then does `run.py:740` call `_stage_step`. For `sample`/`inject` with a live work piece, `_stage_step` prints `run.py: <run_dir> has a live piece; launching nothing` and returns `"stop"` (`run.py:1992-2007`) — no launch. For `train` there is no live-piece guard at all (the guard at `run.py:1992` is `if stage in ("sample", "inject")`), so the walk reaches `launch.launch` and the launch gate refuses on the live session (`jobs/launch.py:239-240`, `:743`) — again no launch, after `last/` and `train_log.jsonl` are already gone. The sentence invites `retry` at a running train job and costs it its checkpoint directory and its log.
problems.fix: In `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:216-218`, state what `retry` does against a live run instead of "launches it again": it clears the markers first and unconditionally (`run.py:739`), then does not launch — `sample`/`inject` stop with `has a live piece; launching nothing`, `train` is refused by the launch gate — so `kill` the run before `retry`. The same sentence's `refire` clause needs the same qualifier: `launch.refire` refuses while the piece's session is alive (`jobs/launch.py:949-951`), which the bullet above already states.

problems.detail: `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:105-109` (rewritten by c17d75c) makes one sentence out of two different outcomes: it names the shape "A piece that starts and then fails its alive check", then says "an `inject` run's probe-service `check` client is the one thing that writes to the terminal on this path, and its `check: ...` lines are the diagnosis". On a real alive-check failure the `check` client never runs and nothing is printed: the service alive check is at `jobs/launch.py:887` and its failure returns at `:888-890`, while the `check` client is started at `jobs/launch.py:895-898`, only after that check passed. The `check: ...` lines (`models/probe_models/service.py:212-261`) belong to the separate `service_check` outcome (`jobs/launch.py:899-901`), which is not an alive-check failure although it ends the same way (teardown, exit 0, `launch_failed` row). A reader hitting the alive-check failure is sent looking for terminal output that does not exist; `jobs/launch.py` has exactly one `print`, at `:955`, in `refire`.
problems.fix: Split the quiet shape's two outcomes in `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:105-109`: a piece failing its alive check prints nothing at all and is read from `<run_dir>/log/<piece index>.txt`; an `inject` run whose `check` client fails its gate prints its own `check: ...` lines. Both exit 0, tear the service pieces down and append the `launch_failed` finish row.

rereview_problems.detail: `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md` Phase 4, the third-shape sentence added by cd980a7, says of the `service_check` outcome: "it ends the same way — teardown, exit 0, `launch_failed` row — and it is the one launch failure that writes to the terminal, so its `check: ...` lines are the diagnosis." That absolute claim is contradicted twice inside the same paragraph. The first shape's own sentence says each of those refusals "prints its own `jobs/launch.py: ...` line and exits 1" (real: `jobs/launch.py:174` dirty tree, `:743` launch gate, `:553`/`:779`/`:795`/`:820` too few free cards — every one a `sys.exit` with a message, which Python writes to stderr), and the fourth shape's own sentence quotes `jobs/launch.py: <path> did not appear within launch_timeout_s` (`jobs/launch.py:672`). So three of the four shapes write to the terminal, not one. The wording the rewrite replaced carried the scope that made the claim true — the old text read "the one thing that writes to the terminal **on this path**" — and the r3 rewrite dropped it while moving the sentence to a different shape. A reader who trusts the sentence literally learns that any `jobs/launch.py:` line on the terminal cannot be a launch failure, which is the opposite of shapes 1 and 4.
rereview_problems.fix: Restore the scope the sentence lost: in the third-shape sentence of `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md` Phase 4, write that it is the one launch failure that ends with exit 0 and still writes to the terminal (or, equally correct, "the one thing that writes to the terminal on this path"), so that shapes 1 and 4, which print their own `jobs/launch.py: ...` line and exit 1, stay outside the claim.

rereview_problems.detail: The message the newly-biting arm produces names no module. `run.py:1031-1033` builds `f"check 2: {current_file} {label}: {subject} importlib.import_module call naming {prefix}<module>{tail}"`, and for a repo-root target `prefix` is the empty string (`_dynamic_import_prefix`, `run.py:941-949`), so the `{prefix}<module>` tail collapses to the literal `<module>`. Measured in a scratch copy of the branch tree: with README giving `run.py` a `used by: eval/method_table.py (by name, inside the table subcommand)` line and `eval/method_table.py` holding `importlib.import_module(f"data.training_data{suffix}")`, selfcheck prints `check 2: run.py used by: by-name entry eval/method_table.py holds no importlib.import_module call naming <module>`, rc=1. For a target inside a package the same tail reads `naming models.probe_models.<module>`, where `<module>` correctly stands for any module of that package; for a root target the required text is one exact dotted name (`run`) and the message hides it, so the operator is told to add a call naming a placeholder. The rr-selfcheck-03 fix text called this out and named `run.py:1029` (now `:1033`) as the same one-expression change; commit 5f455eb changed only the test at `run.py:963`/`:976` and left the message. Minor because the fix itself is correct and no annotation in the tree names a repo-root file by name today, so the line is unreachable on the real tree.
rereview_problems.fix: At `run.py:1033`, make the quoted requirement the text the test actually demands: build the tail from the same value the test uses, e.g. name the module itself when the package prefix is empty — `naming {prefix}<module>` becomes `naming {prefix or _module_name(imported)}` for a root target — so the root-target line reads `... importlib.import_module call naming run` while every package target keeps its present `models.probe_models.<module>` form.
